nodes.definition: A technique applied after training to reduce memory requirements.

nodes.definition: The amount of memory needed by the small transformer model.

nodes.label: retrieval augmented generation
nodes.definition: A method allowing the use of external documents during question answering.

nodes.label: external documents

nodes.label: token embeddings
nodes.definition: Numerical vectors representing individual words or subwords in a sequence.

nodes.label: contextual representations
nodes.definition: Vector representations of tokens that incorporate information from the entire input sequence.

nodes.label: dropout
nodes.definition: A mechanism where random neurons are deactivated during training to prevent co-adaptation of features.

nodes.label: prevents overfitting
nodes.definition: The state or outcome achieved by forcing the network to learn redundant representations that are robust to the absence of specific neurons.

nodes.label: numerical precision of model weights
nodes.definition: The degree of accuracy with which numerical values are represented in a model.

provenance.text: A small transformer uses self-attention to process text and backpropagation to improve its predictions during training. Regularization helps it generalize beyond its training examples. After training, quantization reduces its memory requirements, while retrieval-augmented generation lets it use external documents when answering questions.
